From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-12T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Staged commit playbook for Horus private VPC pilot

Hi Elaine,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday — great alignment on the pilot goals. I attached a first-pass "Staged Commitment Playbook" that lays out a time-boxed evaluation and commercial ramp specifically for a private VPC deployment (see attachment: Staged_Commit_Playbook_v1.pdf). High-level summary: 

- Pilot window: 6 weeks evaluation (technical validation) + 6-month staged production ramp (pilot -> expanded usage).
- Commit tiers and commercial triggers: 3-month ramp milestones (M1/M2/M3) that each unlock incremental discounts and operational commitments (priority capacity, dedicated onboarding).
- Platform fee: can be reduced or waived depending on committed annual spend; we propose a temporary reduced platform fee for the first 90 days of paid pilot if you sign by Nov 30.
- On-prem/VPC license: term licensing with option to transition to perpetual node license or continue as annual commitment; see licensing options table in the attachment.

Ask: please review the playbook and call out any items you want us to tighten up (particularly the milestone KPIs and the license wording). If this looks directionally right, we can produce a revised text (v2) that includes explicit invoice/discount language and a DocuSign-ready term sheet.

Next steps I recommend:
- Elaine: confirm the KPIs you want as M1/M2 (throughput, latency SLOs, token volume).
- If procurement wants pricing detail, we can send a short commercial appendix you can share.

I copied our legal and revenue-ops leads for awareness.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (510) 555-0123
Attachments: Staged_Commit_Playbook_v1.pdf (12 pages, pricing table + milestones)

Tessa — thanks for the playbook and the clear framing. A few clarifying questions from my side and from procurement: 

1) Licensing model: is the on-prem option a term-based license (we keep paying annually) or can it convert to an enterprise perpetual node license after the pilot? We need both variants documented.
2) Platform fee: you mention a waiver depending on committed spend — can you provide the exact thresholds (dollars) and whether that waiver is applied monthly or as an invoice credit?
3) Telemetry & KMS: for compliance we need to confirm what telemetry Redwood collects from a private VPC and whether we can use our HSM/KMS.
4) Evaluation window: can Horus extend the initial evaluation to 60 days (we want a longer systems integration window)?

Procurement also asked for a clear list of deliverables and payment schedule tied to the M1/M2/M3 milestones. We also need the SOW and a draft term sheet we can circulate internally. If possible, can you send a revised playbook that addresses the above?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if that helps.

Elaine Zhang
Head of Cloud & Platform, Horus Analytics
elaine.zhang@horusanalytics.com
Attachments: Horus_NDA.pdf (signed)

Team — forwarding Elaine's questions. Need consensus on what concessions we can offer without setting a precedent. Key asks: 60-day evaluation, detailed thresholds for platform fee waiver, convert-to-perpetual license option, KMS/HSM support details.

My initial thoughts:
- Evaluation: agree to 60 days but tie commercial milestones to an active paid pilot period that starts at the end of eval (so we don't incur open credit exposure).
- Platform fee: propose tiered structure in v2: 100% platform fee for months 0-3 unless signed by Nov 30, 50% platform fee months 4-6, waiver if annual committed ARR >= $650k. Alternatively, offer an upfront credit that amortizes against the platform fee.
- Licensing: allow conversion to perpetual node license with a defined buyout formula at the 12-month mark (one-time conversion fee = 6x monthly commit * node factor).
- KMS/Telemetry: engineering (Marcus) to confirm exact telemetry; we should allow customer-managed KMS in VPC option and document what logs we retain for support.

Laura — can you draft the minimum legal language for the conversion buyout + audit clause? Priya — can you produce a clean invoice schedule that maps to M1/M2/M3?

Thanks — I want to keep this tight; Horus seems eager but price-sensitive.

Subject: Revised: Staged commitment playbook + commercial appendix (v2)

Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Attached is version 2 of the playbook (Staged_Commit_Playbook_v2.pdf) and a short term sheet (Horus_Term_Sheet_v1.docx). Key updates addressing your items: 

- Evaluation window: extended to 60 days (technical evaluation). Paid pilot period begins immediately after evaluation ends; paid pilot duration counts toward M1/M2/M3.
- Platform fee thresholds (applied as invoice credit unless otherwise requested):
  * If annual committed ARR >= $650,000 => full platform fee waiver for first year.
  * If annual committed ARR between $350,000–$650,000 => 50% platform fee credit applied over first 6 months.
  * If committed ARR < $350,000 => standard platform fee (negotiable for multi-year commitment).
- Discounts tied to commit milestones (applied to compute/token unit price):
  * M1 (3 months): 7% off unit price after hitting 40% of committed token volume.
  * M2 (6 months): 12% off unit price after hitting 75% of committed token volume.
  * M3 (12 months): 18% off unit price after sustained ramp and usage SLA compliance.
- Licensing: term license with option to convert to perpetual node license at 12 months. Conversion formula included in the term sheet (one-time buyout formula).
- KMS/Telemetry: private VPC supports customer-managed KMS; telemetry is limited to operational logs necessary for support and aggregated usage metrics (no customer prompt data retained in telemetry). Marcus — please confirm exact log retention windows in the SOW.

Attachments: Staged_Commit_Playbook_v2.pdf (updated milestones & pricing), Horus_Term_Sheet_v1.docx (DocuSign-ready).

If this addresses procurement, we can produce the DocuSign packet (SOW + term sheet) once you confirm the preferred invoice cadence (monthly/quarterly) and whether procurement wants platform fee amortization vs. upfront credit.

Target close: sign SOW by Nov 30 to start setup in mid-December and meet a Jan 15 pilot go-live. If Horus needs an accelerated ramp, we can discuss a partially prepaid commitment to secure capacity.

Best,
Tessa

2) Platform fee waiver threshold: $650k ARR for full waiver is within reason. Can you provide a worked example with sample invoices so we can circulate internally?
3) Conversion formula: procurement asked that the perpetual buyout formula be capped to avoid open-ended exposure; can Laura call that out in a revised clause?

If those items are OK, procurement is comfortable moving to DocuSign review. Adding Patrick (procurement lead) to the thread — he will be the main procurement contact going forward.

Elaine Zhang
